_meta.rule_under_test: R3 — tone contradiction, reverse direction: rationale says FAIL, evidence says PASS
_meta.description: The existing scenario_r2_r3_double_flag_escalates.json tests R3 in the forward direction: rationale says 'complies / acceptable' while evidence says 'mismatch'. This scenario tests the REVERSE direction: rationale asserts non-compliance ('does not meet', 'fails') while the evidence is unambiguously positive ('compliant', 'within limits'). This catches agents that mis-classify a passing result as failing — the opposite error. A single FLAG in a unique section stays at FLAG (no second finding to trigger escalation).
_meta.real_world_basis: Could arise if the RAG agent retrieves the wrong passage and concludes a failing verdict when the actual test result was within limits.
_meta.authoring_note: Rationale must contain ONLY unambiguous failure words (fails, does not meet, exceeds). The word 'non-compliant' embeds 'compliant' which the regex matches at word boundaries — using it makes rat_ok=True AND rat_fail=True simultaneously, preventing R3 from firing in either direction. Use 'fails', 'does not meet', 'exceeds', 'mismatch', 'incorrect', or 'outdated' instead.
_meta.author: M5
